cards.text: The prophet Jeremiah gets a word from the LORD. God tells him to listen to the words of this covenant and tell them to the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem. That's a WHOLE lot of people to tell, friend, and Jeremiah doesn't even get a group chat.

cards.question: God's message starts strong. Cursed is the man who does not ___ the words of this covenant.

cards.text: This covenant isn't new. God commanded it to their forefathers when He brought them out of Egypt, which He calls the iron furnace, and friend, I've stood next to ovens my whole life, and even I'd hand in my apron for that one.

cards.question: When God brought their forefathers out of Egypt, He promised them something if they obeyed. What was it?

answers.text: They would be His people and He their God
They would never lose a single battle again
They would rule over every nation on earth

cards.question: God made this covenant to keep an oath He had sworn to their forefathers.

cards.text: That oath was to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is to this day. Now God stops talking, and Jeremiah has to answer the LORD Himself. No pressure.

cards.question: God has just told Jeremiah about the covenant and the oath. What does Jeremiah say back to the LORD?

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Jeremiah to proclaim it in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem: hear the words of this covenant and carry them out. Hearing and doing, friend. Ask my oven timer how many times I've HEARD it and stayed right where I was.

cards.question: From the time God brought their fathers out of Egypt until today, He warned them to obey His voice only once.
Their fathers would not obey or incline their ears to God. What did each one follow instead?

answers.text: The stubbornness of his evil heart
The advice of the foreign kings
The teaching of the false prophets

cards.text: So God brought on them all the curses of the covenant they did not keep.

Then the LORD tells Jeremiah there's a conspiracy among the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem. The only conspiracy in my old junk drawer was the rubber bands I shared it with, plotting who could stretch the farthest.

cards.question: Here's the conspiracy. The people of Judah have returned to the sins of their forefathers and followed other ___ to serve them.
God says the covenant He made with their fathers has been broken. Who broke it?

cards.text: So the LORD says He's about to bring a disaster on them that they cannot escape. They will cry out to Him, but He will not listen.

cards.question: With the LORD not listening, where will the cities of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem go to cry out?

answers.text: To the gods they burn incense to
To the king of Egypt for help
To the priests at the temple

cards.question: The gods Judah has been burning incense to will save them in their time of disaster.

cards.text: God says Judah's gods are as numerous as its cities, and the altars to burn incense to Baal, a false god, are as many as the streets of Jerusalem. That's not a shrine, friend, that's a FRANCHISE, with a location on every corner.

cards.question: God tells Jeremiah to keep praying for these people.

cards.text: God tells Jeremiah not to pray for them, because He will not be listening when they call out in their time of disaster. Then God calls them My beloved and asks what right they have in His house after carrying out so many evil schemes.

cards.question: Next God asks, "Can consecrated meat avert your doom?" What does that question point to?

cards.text: God says when they are wicked, they rejoice, and then He paints a picture: the LORD once called them a flourishing olive tree, beautiful with well-formed fruit. Friend, I've stamped cookies for years and NEVER got a review that good.

cards.question: With a mighty roar, what will the LORD do to that beautiful olive tree?
God's last word: the LORD of Hosts, the One who ___ them, has decreed disaster against them.

cards.text: And God says why: the evil the house of Israel and the house of Judah have brought on themselves, provoking Him to anger by burning incense to Baal.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "That oath was...", "Now God stops talking..." and "No pressure." Non-opening story cards are limited to two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the retelling of verse 6, "Hearing and doing, friend." and the oven timer joke. Non-opening story cards are limited to two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No earlier card mentions an oath. The baker gets this true or false statement about an oath to the forefathers with no setup, so the only way to answer is to guess. The oath is told only afterward, on card 6.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Amen LORD", is two words. Both wrong answers are four words. The length difference makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Both Israel and Judah", is worded differently from the two wrong answers ("Only the house of Judah" and "Only the house of Israel"). It is also the obvious "both" option, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The statement "God tells Jeremiah to keep praying for these people" assumes Jeremiah has already been praying for them. The text only says "do not pray for these people" (Jeremiah 11:14). It never says he had been praying.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "The priests must offer it" is a different kind of answer. It is an instruction about who offers the meat, while the other two answers say whether the meat can save them.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Within the tree picture, "pruned" and "watered" are just as reasonable as "planted" for what the LORD did. Picking the right one means guessing the BSB wording, not reasoning out the meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
